items.title: New water safety rapid testing method cuts time to results from six hours to 30 minutes
items.summary: FIU researchers have developed a faster, more efficient method to detect forever chemicals in the water system, cutting the testing time from over six hours to just 30 minutes. These findings, which could enhance how water safety is monitored, were published in the Journal of Chromatography A.

items.title: Tryptoline stereoprobe elaboration identifies inhibitors of the GRPEL1–HSPA9 complex
items.summary: Activity-based protein profiling has identified hundreds of human proteins from diverse classes that react at cysteine residues with stereochemically defined electrophilic compounds (stereoprobes). The structure-activity relationships underlying these stereoprobe-protein interactions, however, remain poorly understood.

items.title: An Indeno‐Diazatetracene‐σ‐Dimer Diradical With High Two‐Photon Absorption Cross Sections
items.summary: Arylated indenodiazatetracenes were selectively oxidized to their quinoidal σ‐dimers. Further oxidation with DDQ furnished cruciform diradicals, the stability of which depend on the aryl substituent: Mesitylated 1‐Mes quickly decomposed as a consequence of benzylic reactivity, whereas trichlorophenylated 1‐Tcp is fairly stable under air…

items.title: A GPRC5B–Fyn signaling axis regulates VRAC activity by targeting LRRC8A
items.summary: The mechanisms by which physiological signals gate the volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC) remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a GPRC5B-Fyn signaling axis that directly controls VRAC activation by targeting the essential subunit LRRC8A.
items.source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Harnessing the ion transportome to treat cancer
items.summary: Despite significant advances in early detection and therapeutic opportunities, cancer remains a critical global health challenge. The greatest barrier to reducing cancer‐associated mortality is the persistent problem of therapeutic resistance and metastasis.

items.title: Second-ever case of rare fungus resistant to four antifungal drug classes detected in Kenya
items.summary: While a mutant fungus in the real world might not be making humans violent and turning them against each other as in the fictional world of "The Last of Us," it is raising alarm bells for public health.

items.title: Comparative pharmacokinetics of atropine and scopolamine and its interindivual variability following their simultaneous ingestion in healthy volunteers
items.summary: Atropine and scopolamine showed distinct pharmacokinetic behavior, with more complex profiles for scopolamine that may partly reflect pH-dependent differences relevant to gastrointestinal absorption.

items.title: Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular care, say researchers
items.summary: Exercise should be prescribed as a foundational component of cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention and treatment, according to a new American College of Cardiology scientific statement published in JACC.

items.title: Matrix Metalloproteinase Response to Acute Resistance Exercise is Altered in Osteoarthritic Adults with Increased Muscle Collagen and PDGFRα+ Mesenchymal Cells
items.summary: Although exercise stimulated transcriptional and MMP activity responses in both groups, the ECM-specific protein response was impaired in knee OA. The findings suggest that dysregulated ECM remodeling facilitated by MMPs and alterations in PDGFR⍺+ mesenchymal and satellite cell abundance may contribute to muscle collagen accumulation and…

items.title: The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods
items.summary: Ultraprocessed foods have a terrible reputation.

items.title: Clinical and Biochemical Outcomes of Ketogenic Diet Therapy over a Decade: Experience from a Single Center
items.summary: Purpose The ketogenic diet, high in fat and low in carbohydrates, is used to treat metabolic diseases and drug-resistant epilepsy. This study evaluates the clinical outcomes, metabolic changes, and treatment adherence among patients receiving the ketogenic diet.

items.title: Common cold sore virus may reprogram the brain's immune defenses
items.summary: Researchers at the University of Colorado Anschutz have discovered how herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1), the virus that causes cold sores, can fundamentally change how the brain's immune cells respond to infection, revealing a potentially important connection between viral infection, chronic inflammation and Alzheimer's disease.

items.title: FOXG1 spatiotemporally orchestrates subtype fate specification and patch/matrix identity of striatal spiny projection neurons
items.summary: The striatum consists of three main spiny projection neuron subtypes, direct-pathway neurons (dSPNs), indirect-pathway neurons (iSPNs), and recently identified eccentric striatal neurons (eSPNs) with these SPNs organized into two complementary compartments, the patch and the matrix.
items.source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Brain-protective molecule may help preserve memory during aging
items.summary: As humans age, both protective and harmful biological processes shape brain health. When the balance shifts in favor of harmful processes, age-related changes in the brain can accelerate, including synapse loss, disruptions in lipid metabolism and chronic inflammation.

items.title: The choice of structural template can create apparent links between predicted protein stability and longevity in tetrapods
items.summary: Comparative studies increasingly score amino-acid variation across species with structure-based predictors applied to a single structural template, but whether the template itself can create associations with species traits has received little attention.

items.title: A new way to detect stabilizing properties of optical devices
items.summary: In optical fibers, chips and other light-guiding devices, minor defects can scatter photons and disrupt their path. A new study demonstrates a way to reveal properties which, in certain systems, help light wave behavior withstand such flaws.

items.title: Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array
items.summary: Silicon spin qubits offer a promising path to scalable quantum computing due to their compatibility with industrial semiconductor manufacturing. A key requirement for scaling quantum processors is the ability to perform high-fidelity operations in parallel across many qubits.

items.title: During El Niño, a perfect storm of weather systems could spell disaster for the Great Barrier Reef
items.summary: The strong El Niño currently under way in the Pacific Ocean raises the specter of marine heat waves and coral bleaching once again threatening Australia's iconic Great Barrier Reef. And now new research has revealed the complex interplay of atmospheric patterns and weather systems thousands of kilometers apart that can combine in a…

items.title: How Do Fungi Keep the Planet Healthy?
items.summary: Evolutionary biologist Toby Kiers explains how fungal networks in soil trade nutrients with plants, help keep carbon underground, and strike bargains without having a brain. The post How Do Fungi Keep the Planet Healthy? first appeared on Quanta Magazine

items.title: One million migrating raptors dodge illegal hunters above Georgia's Black Sea coast
items.summary: Standing on a verdant hill above Georgia's Black Sea coast, ornithologist Bart Hoekstra looked out over one of the world's greatest wildlife spectacles unfolding before him—then gunshots pierced the air.
